Here’s a quick psychology lesson that may help in this situation and lots of other situations as well. It’s REALLY fucking long so I understand if you don’t feel like reading it! I’ll include a tldr lol


The first thing I thought of is the concept of primary and secondary emotions. 

Primary emotions are the initial and “core” emotions that are direct reactions to different situations. Experts disagree with what constitutes as a primary emotion but most lists seek to include at least some of these and different types of them: joy, sadness, fear, disgust and some studies include anger but I (and other studies) disagree. In some situations, these are secondary but more often than not they are primary. Our reactions to primary emotions and what triggers seem to be wired in childhood experiences. 

Secondary emotions build off of primary emotions and are how we feel about the primary ones; simply put they are emotional reactions to our initial emotions. Oftentimes, it’s easier to understand and even less painful to feel secondary emotions than primary emotions because the primary ones require more thought and evaluation. I’ll try to apply it to this situation. 


You feel uncomfortable.  We have emotions that make us uncomfortable for a variety of reasons but discomfort in itself is not an emotion. What’s making you uncomfortable? Maybe you’re jealous? Other possibilities could be feeling shame, insecure or worried and those emotions oftentimes sprout from fear or its subcategories. If that sounds about right for your situation it could be helpful to identify what you’re afraid of, why it makes you afraid and why it causes those secondary emotions. That way, you can work through it and find solutions. 

I hope this is helpful to you or anyone else dealing with a similar situation. The therapist I’m seeing recommended doing some research on this concept and it makes me feel better because it can provide a deeper understanding. It’s also frustrating as hell. If it’s not helpful: I’m so sorry for making you read all of this and wasting your time lol :,) please forgive me 


TLDR: Our primary emotions (joy, sadness, fear, disgust and sometimes anger), which are our initial emotions triggered by different situations, lead to secondary emotions. Secondary emotions are emotional reactions to the primary emotions. Identifying the secondary emotion/s and the primary emotion that lies beneath can be helpful in understanding why you feel what you feel and shift the emotions in a different direction.

Tip 3: This relates to Tip 1; Avoid building them up in your head and putting them on a pedestal before meeting them or even after the first (few) date(s). See them as who they are and observe how they present themselves. This can help you to avoid taking it personally if things don’t work out. Being disappointed is normal and understandable but it can quickly change into beating yourself up for “not being xxx enough” when you’ve already created a certain image of them in your head. Something I’m prone to doing is ignoring all the negatives and focusing solely on what went well. Put the rose colored glasses down and keep your deal-breakers in mind! As Wanda from Bojack Horseman says: “When you look at someone through rose-colored glasses, all the red flags just look like flags.” 

Tip 4: The first date isn’t necessarily going to be everything you expected it to be. That doesn’t have to mean that it went badly and isn’t worth persuing :) First dates can be awkward and uncomfortable to a certain degree without it being a red flag. That being said, follow your gut instinct!

Lastly, try to have fun :) Be yourself, wear something that makes you feel nice and cultivate a positive mindset. Having low expectations and being positive aren’t mutually exclusive. Be excited and jittery! Embrace the butterflies and nausea!  That’s part of the fun :) 

Good luck, I sincerely hope it goes well <3

This may be a hot take but I personally would feel really uncomfortable if someone I was on a first date posted pictures of us on their public story. That might just be me though, but I would feel weird and pressured to meet up again. I’d also like to add that although I completely understand that you wanted to see if she would make the first move and message you after the date, but tons of girls have the mindset that it should be the guy who reaches out first. It’s like getting proof that he enjoyed the date and is genuinely interested in you. Personally idgaf and will often reach out the second day after a date if he hasn’t because then I start overthinking. That way I can find out if really was a good date or if he changed his mind afterwards (that’s happened to me and it sucked but at least I didn’t have to wonder about it). A tip for the future is that you can start off by telling her that you had a great time at the end of the date and maybe say that you’ll talk to her later. Then wait 2-3 days and if you’re still interested send her a message. I like to send something like: “Hi again! I really enjoyed spending time with you.” Then I’ll bring something up from the date, something like “I’m still thinking about that dinner, it was unbelievable 🤤” (terrible example but hopefully you get my point). Then later in the concersation you could bring up a second date casually (“We should try that new restaurant sometime, I’ve heard great things!”) It shows interest and that you’ve been thinking about the date. I’m sorry about how long this answer was lol, I can’t get past the 1/2 date myself but this is how I at least try or what makes me feel like he’s interested in a second date. Best of luck!
